claims.text: Implementing hierarchical microstructures in high-entropy alloys will enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering from hierarchical microstructures will reduce thermal conductivity relative to conventional microstructures.
A hierarchical arrangement of microstructural features disrupts phonon-transport pathways.
Disruption of phonon-transport pathways increases phonon-scattering events.
Increased phonon scattering reduces thermal conductivity.
High-entropy alloys with hierarchical microstructures will have at least 20% lower thermal conductivity than comparable alloys with conventional microstructures.
The prediction is intended to apply at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys designed for thermal-insulation applications.
The hypothesis may not extend to other material classes or applications.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity reduction may vary with alloy composition.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity reduction may vary with microstructural design.
The hypothesis is falsified if hierarchical specimens do not show at least a 20% thermal-conductivity reduction relative to conventional-microstructure controls measured under identical conditions.
